component: Response to the independent Opus review of unit hw-profiles' first submission (all 12 findings)

preregistration.written_after_fix_note: Preregistered the fix plan for each finding before implementing it in this round; this file records outcome and disposition per finding after the fixes landed.
preregistration.expectation: Every blocker and major finding gets a code, data or test change; every minor finding gets either a fix or an explicit, evidenced reason it is out of scope (a protected path); no finding is silently dropped.
preregistration.criteria: This file lists all 12 findings from the review with a disposition (fixed / addressed / out_of_scope_protected_path) and points to the concrete diff or receipt for each.

acceptance_check_ref: tests/test_hardware_profile.py, tests/test_workflow_hardening.py, tests/test_workflow_security_coverage.py, actionlint, zizmor --offline (all re-run after the fixes; see hardware-profile-tool.json and mlx-lm-hash-lock.json for the detailed command/result records)
results: blocker (macOS venv/uv discovery): fixed. .github/workflows/hardware-profile-smoke.yml no longer activates the venv or invokes `python3 -m uv`; uv is a standalone downloaded binary ($UV) called directly, and `uv pip install --python <venv>/bin/python3 --require-hashes` targets the venv interpreter without needing uv importable inside it. See mlx-lm-hash-lock.json.

major (unreproducible redundant-compile diff): fixed. Both the committed lock generation and the CI diff-check recompile now pass --exclude-newer 2026-09-23T00:00:00Z; verified byte-identical to the already-committed lock file across two independent re-runs at that cutoff. See mlx-lm-hash-lock.json.

major (WSL effective_ram_gb wrongly preferred .wslconfig over measured /proc/meminfo): fixed. scripts/hardware_profile.py's new _effective_ram_gb() prefers /proc/meminfo (native_proven) and only falls back to the .wslconfig value (source_review) when meminfo could not be read; on this host that moves embedding_semantic_rag_tier from 'full' to 'standard' (47.0 GB measured vs. the 48 GB threshold). See hardware-profile-tool.json and the regenerated this-host.json.

major (macOS unified memory treated as 100% usable VRAM, double-counted against the RAG tier): addressed with a labelled, conservative fix, not a measurement. adoption/hardware-profiles.json now declares macos_unified_gpu_working_set_fraction=0.6 (explicitly labelled as a conservative assumption, not Apple's undocumented default), applied only to the unified-memory VRAM estimate; a 48GB Mac now resolves to 'large-32b-q4' instead of 'unified-70b-plus'. A concurrent_use_warning field is set whenever a unified-memory host's generation and RAG tiers are both non-trivial, documenting that the two budgets are sequential-use estimates, not a verified concurrent-use accounting (exact joint accounting was judged out of proportion to a labelled-projection host with no macOS execution available to validate it).
major (github-macos-15-arm64-runner marked native_proven with no values): fixed. Its evidence_class is now 'pending' with an evidence field stating no CI artifact exists yet.

major (ecosystem_bounded_run mismatched the wrapper's actual MemoryHigh/MemoryMax interface and was 4x the default): fixed. The layer now emits ecosystem_job_memory_high_gb/ecosystem_job_memory_max_gb, named after the exact ECOSYSTEM_JOB_MEMORY_HIGH/ECOSYSTEM_JOB_MEMORY_MAX env vars the wrapper reads, sized as max(default_max_gb=6, ram*0.25) capped at 32 (down from an uncapped half-of-RAM rule), with the wrapper's own 4G/6G defaults stated as the WSL-stability containment floor this is a bounded, opt-in ceiling raise on top of, not a replacement for.
minor (pull_request path filter omitted tools/mlx-smoke/run_smoke.py): fixed. Added to the paths list.

minor (uv installed via unverified `pip install --user`): fixed as part of the blocker fix -- uv is now downloaded from GitHub Releases and SHA-256-verified, matching validate.yml's pattern for the Linux uv install.

minor (handbook describes this host's CPU model without measuring it): fixed. scripts/hardware_profile.py now reads /proc/cpuinfo's 'model name' on Linux/WSL (cpu_brand field); this host's actual measured value is 'Intel(R) Core(TM) Ultra 9 275HX', matching the brief's claim, now backed by a measurement instead of an assertion. The handbook's Hardware profiles section was reworded to say 'measured' explicitly.

minor (this-host.json redaction not labelled): fixed. Added a top-level _redaction_note field stating exactly what was changed (the Windows username in wslconfig_source) and that it is a post-run edit, not raw script output.

minor (mlx-lm-hash-lock.json preregistration looked written after the fact): acknowledged, not further fixed. This response file and both revised receipts are honest about being written after their fixes in this round (see written_after_fix_note in each); the original receipt's ordering cannot be retroactively proven and is not being re-asserted as prior.

minor (run_smoke.py's tokens/s was a wall-clock estimate; unverified revision SHA; unverified load() revision= support): fixed. run_smoke.py now uses mlx_lm.generate.stream_generate's GenerationResponse (generation_tps, peak_memory, generation_tokens) directly instead of computing an estimate. The pinned HF revision SHA was confirmed to exist via Hugging Face's revision API. mlx_lm 0.30.2's load() signature was confirmed (by inspecting the downloaded PyPI sdist) to accept revision=. See mlx-lm-hash-lock.json for the exact commands/results.

minor (test_hardware_profile.py did not cover detect_nvidia_gpu, measure_macos, or WSL RAM substitution; macOS path never run): fixed for the first two -- both are now covered with mocked subprocess output (DetectNvidiaGpuTests, MeasureMacosTests) and the WSL RAM-source logic is extracted into a pure, directly-tested _effective_ram_gb() (EffectiveRamGbTests). The macOS code path still has never executed on a real macOS host; that remains an open limit, not fixable from this Linux worktree, and is why hardware-profile-smoke.yml's macOS job exists.

minor (_find_wslconfig silently picks the alphabetically-first multi-user profile): improved, not eliminated. _find_all_wslconfigs() now returns every match and measure_linux reports the others as wslconfig_other_candidates so the ambiguity is visible in the JSON output; the script still auto-picks the first one (no signal to determine the 'right' profile without invoking a Windows binary, which the module's read-only design avoids). Left as a documented limit.

minor (handbook still conflates Codex CLI 0.155.1 and the Codex SDK openai-codex 0.154.0 at lines 546 and 581): confirmed out of scope for this unit. Both lines fall inside the <!-- verdicts:begin/end --> generated block (537-2265), which this unit's brief explicitly forbids editing. The review's own finding agrees the unit was correct to leave the block alone and asks only that the residual be recorded here for a unit with permission to touch the generator's source data (catalogs/sota-convergence/manifest-*.json, also on this unit's do-not-touch list) to pick up.
limits: This file is a disposition summary, not itself an executed check; the underlying re-run evidence is in hardware-profile-tool.json and mlx-lm-hash-lock.json.

The macOS-unified-memory-fraction and ecosystem_bounded_run-fraction constants (0.6, 0.25, 32-cap) are this unit's own judgment calls responding to the review's qualitative findings, not independently re-derived from a cited Apple/systemd specification; they are labelled as assumptions in adoption/hardware-profiles.json for exactly this reason.
Two findings (Codex CLI/SDK conflation in the generated block; multi-user .wslconfig auto-pick) are explicitly not eliminated -- see their entries above for why.
